pub(all) enum TypeId {

43 more, listed under variants below.

The internal type ID: the byte that begins a value's type meta, and the number every language agrees on.

The numbers are the specification's, and they are not ours to choose: a reader in Go reads 21 as a string because the type mapping says so. The variant names are the specification's too, except NoneType, which Python calls NoneType and the table calls NONE; MoonBit spells nothing None, so the spelling here is Python's.

fn TypeId::arrayed(Self) -> Self?

The dense array of this element type, when there is one.

Only the fourteen element types above have one; array<string> stays a list, which is why the answer is optional.

Whether the width of this type is decided by the value rather than by the type: the compressed integers, which sort after every fixed-width one.

Whether this kind is one of the dense primitive arrays: a run of raw little-endian elements rather than a list of values.

is_named_by_id

fn TypeId::is_named_by_id(Self) -> Bool

Whether this kind is one of the five that hold a user type ID in same-schema mode: the four that a struct can be, and the enum.

is_primitive

fn TypeId::is_primitive(Self) -> Bool

Whether a field of this type belongs to the primitive groups when the field order is decided: numbers and booleans, not strings and not containers.

is_user

fn TypeId::is_user(Self) -> Bool

Whether a value of this kind names a type of the writer's own, and so carries a user type ID or type meta after the type ID byte.

These are the kinds a field must write type information for. An enum or a union inside a struct field does not: its type is the field's declared one.

kind

fn TypeId::kind(Self) -> @moonmodel.Type

The kind a type ID stands for, which is how a wire type is described to a projection that has never heard of this format.

The widths collapse — every signed 32-bit type is Int, every 64-bit one a Big — because the description is not the place a width is decided. What the vocabulary has no word for is a Raw naming the wire type, which is what Raw is for; nothing reads inside it, and the wire record beside the description still holds the type ID itself.

of

fn TypeId::of(Int32) -> Self?

The type a number on the wire stands for, when the mapping has one.

57 and up are unmapped: the specification reserves them, and a reader that met one could not know what to build.

of_kind

fn TypeId::of_kind(@moonmodel.Type) -> Self raise

The type ID a kind goes out as.

The widths are the compact ones — a field that is Int goes out as a VARINT32 and a Big as a VARINT64 — because that is what every peer's own mapping table chooses for the same word, and a field only interoperates when the two sides agree on the type ID as well as on the value.

A kind the format cannot carry — Any, which has no type ID at all — is refused by name.
